title: Optimization of Diagnostic Instruments for Migraine – Project II
summary:
Migraine is a frequent headache disorder. About 14-15% of people worldwide are affected (Steiner & Stovner, 2023). Migraine leads to a high burden and a reduced quality of life (Ashina et al., 2021). Psychological factors (e.g., stress, anxiety) are considered to affect the course of the disease. Therefore, the assessment of migraine should include psychological factors as well as disease-related disability. Psychological questionnaires („scales“) can be used to support migraine-assessment. There are self-report questionnaires for the following issues:
- headache-related disability
- emotional burden
- factors influencing the activity of the disease
- coping with the disease

The assessment of these issues allows for a more tailored treatment of migraine. The project "Optimization of Diagnostic Instruments for Migraine" (ODIN-Migraine) aims to expand the repertoire of questionnaires for the behavioral assessment in migraine. In the already finished ODIN-Migraine I research project, two questionnaires were developed: (i) the Fear of Attacks in Migraine Inventory (FAMI, Klan et al., 2022) and (ii) a German version of the Cogniphobia Scale for Headache Disorders (CS-HD, Klan et al., 2024). Both questionnaires allow the assessment of migraine-related fears (here: attack anxiety or cogniphobia). Attack anxiety is the fear of the occurrence of a migraine or headache attack. Cogniphobia is the fear of mental exertion, which is believed to precipitate or exacerbate headache (Seng and Klepper, 2017).

Aim of the current research project, ODIN-Migraine II, is to continue ODIN-Migraine I. In doing so, ODIN-Migraine II will focus on two different questionnaires:
(i) the 15-items CS-HD from ODIN-Migraine I (Klan et al., 2024; Seng & Klepper, 2017), and 
(ii) the Migraine Interictal Burden Scale (MIBS-4, Buse et al., 2007). The MIBS-4 uses 4 items to assess the burden in the attack-free period (interictal = between attacks). The development of a German-language version of the MIBS-4 was completed before this project.

The quality ("psychometric properties") of both questionnaires (CS-HD and MIBS-4, each the German version) is to be determined. The objective of ODIN-Migraine II is to evaluate the efficacy of both questionnaires in accurately capturing changes. Additionally, the determination of a cut-off is intended (a cut-off may serve as a decision aid for a treatment indication).
The data collection will be carried out in a headache clinic, using a pre-post design (assessment at the beginning and four weeks after inpatient treatment ended). The assessment is provided via an online survey of patients with migraine. The survey will be conducted through the SoSci-Survey portal and will take approximately 25 minutes each.

interventions.name: Routine inpatient treatment at the Migraine and Headache Clinic Königstein

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Diagnosed migraine (episodic migraine with/without aura or chronic migraine) according to criteria 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 of the International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD-3, 3rd Edition, 2018, Headache Classification Committee of the International Headache Society, IHS).
• Current treatment at the Migraine and Headache Clinic Königstein.
• Duration of disease of at least 12 months.
Exclusion criteria:
None
